skills.description: Evaluate the artifact before reading the maker's account of it, and write your findings before opening their notes. Use for every review, evaluation, fact-check or QA pass.
Treat every factual sentence a user will see as a claim with an address, a kind of support and a source, verified by someone other than its author. Use when building content that states facts.
Record a decision with its owner, date, status, the options, the reason and the objections that travel with it. Use for any decision another role will rely on (architecture, org, budget, product).

Build a page for a company's HQ (or a template for the city's pages/) from the HQ's contracts only (events, org, dashboard, knowledge, documents), never from the company's files. Use when a company needs a view the starter pages do not have.
Get work onto main only through the referee (the test suite, a held-out set, a judge script), so main never gets worse. Use for every change to a product that has a referee.

Record a meeting's minutes (title, room, chair, attendees, decisions, objections, a summary and the record it wrote) as an event the HQ shows in Meetings and Rooms. Use whenever two or more roles meet to decide something.
Commit predictions before a run, an experiment or a launch, then judge the result against them (wrong ones included). Use whenever work will produce a number someone will read as success or failure.

Leave what you learned as knowledge entries (practice, finding, dead end, pitfall) with evidence and a belief from 0 to 1, so the next member starts where you stopped. Use when leaving a run, after a surprising result, or when off-boarding.
